name: Huawei GaussDB
tagline: Huawei's distributed enterprise RDBMS built on openGauss, aimed at replacing Oracle in Chinese finance.
description: GaussDB is Huawei's commercial relational database, available as a Huawei Cloud service and as on-premises software, in centralized and distributed (shared-nothing) deployments. Its kernel is the same lineage as the open-source openGauss, which itself started from PostgreSQL 9.2 but has diverged heavily (thread model, Ustore engine, MOT in-memory tables). Huawei markets it for 'two-city, three-centre' high availability, Oracle and MySQL compatibility modes and PB-scale clusters, and it is widely adopted by Chinese banks under the domestic-technology push. 2026 updates added a native vector retrieval engine and cross-page compression. Outside China, availability, documentation and ecosystem are limited.

pricing.notes: Pay-per-use or yearly/monthly on Huawei Cloud; on-premises via enterprise contracts.

scale.notes: Distributed edition documented at 1,000+ nodes and PB-scale storage, with cross-AZ and cross-city DR.

strengths: Distributed shared-nothing edition scales to very large clusters with strong consistency
Oracle- and MySQL-compatibility modes ease migration of existing applications
Cross-AZ and multi-city disaster recovery designed for bank regulators
Same lineage as open-source openGauss, so skills partially transfer
weaknesses: Mainly available on Huawei Cloud and in China; limited global presence
Documentation and community are predominantly Chinese
Heavily diverged from PostgreSQL, so most PG extensions do not apply
useCases: Core banking replacement of Oracle in China
Government and telecom systems under domestic-technology mandates
Large distributed OLTP on Huawei Cloud
notIdealFor: Deployments on AWS, Azure or GCP
Teams relying on the PostgreSQL extension ecosystem
